transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I guess I'm here because the clinic got on me about how little I’ve been eating lately. They made me make this appointment. 

Most days I’m just grabbing a coffee before my shift at the warehouse, and then maybe I'll have a yogurt or just a few bites of something after my GED class. It's just... sitting down for a real meal feels like it throws off everything I’m trying to keep in line. So, yeah, that's why they sent me.
When you avoid eating, is it because you are specifically worried about gaining weight?

Yeah, pretty much. Like, if I eat something heavy... say, some fried food from the break room at work, or a big plate of something at church... I just get really scared that it’s going to show on me right away. I'll just keep thinking about it for the rest of the day, and it makes me want to go check the scale to make sure. So it's just easier to avoid it.
Do you ever find that you lose control over your eating and consume an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

No, not really. Um, I don't ever just sit down and eat a whole bunch of food at once. Losing control like that isn't really something that happens to me. Like I was saying, I mostly just stick to my coffee or a few small bites, so... no, I don't do that.
Could you tell me how much you currently weigh and how that compares to your height?

Um, I'm not exactly sure what my exact weight is right now. I know I'm about five foot four, but I haven't actually stepped on a scale in the last few days, so... I couldn't give you a specific number.
When you look at yourself in a mirror, or when others comment on your appearance, do people often mention that you look very thin or frail?

Yeah, people do say things like that. Like, my work pants are pretty loose on me right now, and some of the people at work will tell me I look too thin. 

But... I don't know. Even with them saying that, and my clothes being big, when I see the number go down I just feel like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don't really see it as looking frail. So I just don’t see why I should be pushed to put the weight back on when I'm actually making progress.
Since you have been losing weight, have your menstrual periods stopped or become irregular?
Um, I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't been keeping track of them lately. I guess I just haven't noticed if they've changed or stopped.
Could you tell me approximately what you weigh right now so I can understand how your weight compares to what would be expected for someone of your height?

Like I said a minute ago, I honestly don't know. I haven't been on a scale in a few days, so... I really just don't have an exact number or even a good guess to give you right now. I know I'm five foot four, but that's really all I can tell you for sure.
When you last stepped on a scale, even if it was a few days ago, what was the number you saw?
I... I really don't remember exactly. I know you're trying to figure it out, but I just don't have a number in my head right now. I just know my clothes are loose, like I said.
When you last weighed yourself, was your weight below 115 pounds?

Look, I don't want to focus on the exact number. But... my work pants are really loose, and yeah, people keep telling me I look too thin. Honestly, though, when I see the number go down, it just feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. I really don’t see why I should be pushed to put the weight back on.
Aside from restricting your food intake, do you engage in any other behaviors to try to control your weight, such as exercising excessively or using anything to help you lose weight?

No, I don't do any of that. I mean... I don't take any pills or use anything like that to lose weight. And I don't really work out, besides just being on my feet all day at work packing boxes. That tires me out enough as it is. So, no, it's really just... just being careful about the food.
When you look at your own body, do you feel like you are actually overweight, even though others are telling you that you look too thin?

Yeah, I do. When I look in the mirror, like before heading to work, my stomach and my thighs... they just still look bigger than they should. People can say what they want, but that's what I see. And honestly, how they look basically decides everything for me. It makes me feel like I’m either doing good or just completely failing for the whole rest of the day.
